title: ME498 (Mechanical Design Optimization): Bike Frame Topology Optimization
summary: I developed a Python-based SIMP topology optimization model to explore aluminum bike frame designs under cruising, off-saddle climbing, and braking loads. Using the finite element method, analytical sensitivities, and SciPy's SLSQP optimizer, I minimized compliance while limiting material to 30% of the fully solid design domain. The resulting 2D designs revealed how different riding conditions change the optimal placement of material and frame reinforcement.
imageAlt: Results slide comparing optimized bike frame density maps for cruising, climbing, and braking, with corresponding cycling photographs.
